segments.he: הלכה א. האונאה שתות ע"פ מ"ש רבינו נ"י סי' ר"פ על פ' כי תצא בחי' מו"מ באמונה. כי המו"מ לברר הנצוצות וזה נעשה ע"י האמונה, שעשוה המו"מ באמונה ע"ש. וצריך לדבק פנימיות מחשבתו בשעת המו"מ אל תורה ועי"ז מקבלת האמונה כח לברר הנצוצות ע"ש. וזה בחי' חב"ד דעשי' עולה אל היצירה שהוא ו' שהוא התורה עי' שם כ"ז היטב:
segments.en: The matter of inheritance to the children, and the essential inheritance belongs to the male son specifically; and if he has no son, “and you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter,” etc. And the principle that emerges for our subject is that guarding the bris [covenant] consists of two aspects: bris ilah [the upper covenant] and bris tatah [the lower covenant], which are the tzaddik and the lamdan [Torah scholar]. These are the aspect of: “the angel of Hashem of Hosts” (Malachi 2:7). “Angel” — this is the aspect of the lamdan, the aspect of Metatron, who comprises the six orders of Mishnah, the aspect of bris tatah. And the tzaddik in good deeds — this is the aspect of bris ilah, the aspect of “Hashem of Hosts — He is a sign in His host,” etc. — see there. And through guarding the bris, through this one merits kisufin d'kedushah [holy yearnings] — to yearn and to long constantly for Hashem, blessed be He. And through this, one makes nefashos [souls]. For holy yearnings are exceedingly precious, for through them one makes holy souls. And through this, nekudos [vowel points] are made for the letters, in the aspect of: “points of silver” (Shir HaShirim 1:11). For the nekudos relative to the letters are in the aspect of the soul relative to the body — for the nekudos direct the letters, pair them, and combine them. For without the nekudos, the letters have no form, no movement, and no combination — just as the body has no vitality and no movement without the soul. And these souls, which are the aspect of nekudos, are made through holy yearnings — through which the letters are formed for good. And conversely, the opposite, G–d forbid — see there. And through meriting to make souls through holy yearnings, through this, all one's eating is in the aspect of lechem hapanim [showbread/bread of the Face]. And then all the stars and constellations and all the nations of the world toil for the sake of his parnasah, etc., etc. And this is the aspect of: “My Face shall go” (Shemos 33:14). For eating and parnasah are the aspect of halichah [going], the aspect of raglayim [feet], etc. And when they ascend to the aspect of Panim [Face], through this: “And I shall give you rest.” For the table atones like the altar, etc. — see all this there well. And this is the aspect of the inheritance that belongs to his children after him. For all the children that one merits to beget and to leave behind as a blessing are in the aspect of tikkun habris. For the essential tikkun habris is to multiply and to beget offspring to sustain the world, as it is written: “I am Keil Shaddai; be fruitful and multiply” (Bereishis 35:11). Keil Shaddai — this is the aspect of tikkun habris, which is called Shaddai, as is known — and its repair is the aspect of “be fruitful and multiply,” to beget children in the world. And these children that one begets are in the aspect of the nefashos that are made through tikkun habris, as above in the Torah mentioned above. And therefore, one must sanctify oneself greatly during marital relations — to exert oneself to detach one's thought from physical desires, from bodily desires, and to attach one's thought only to kisufin d'kedushah toward Hashem, blessed be He, in order to draw a holy soul to one's children, as is explained in the Holy Zohar. And the principle is that all souls emerge from the aspect of the bris, which is the passage through which all souls pass, as is explained in the Holy Zohar. And one who guards the bris merits to beget holy souls, for one merits kisufin d'kedushah constantly, through which holy souls are born at all times — which are the aspect of nekudos for the letters. And then certainly, also when one merits to beget actual children, one certainly draws to them a holy soul, for one is separated and distinguished from bodily desires — only one's thought is attached to Hashem, blessed be He, in kisufin d'kedushah toward Him, blessed be He, alone.

segments.he: והנה יצירה הוא בחי' מט"ט שהוא ו' שהוא בחי' ששה סדרי משנה שמברר הדין כשר ופסול טמא וטהור אסור ומותר. וע"כ משם מקבלת האמונה כח לברר הנצוצות כי בירור הנצוצות הוא בחי' לברר הטוב מן הרע כידוע וזה נעשה דייקא ע"י התורה דהיינו ע"י שמבררין הדין הכשר ופסול וכו', עי"ז יכולין לברר הטוב מן הרע שזהו בירור הנצוצות וכמובא מזה בדברי רבינו נ"י סי' ח'. והנה כשמאנה ומטעה את חבירו הוא פוגם באמונהו אין המו"מ באמונה כי רימה והטעה את חבירו, וע"כ השיעור שתות בחי' ו' שהוא בחי' התורה שמשם מקבלת האמונה כנ"ל. וע"כ שתות מחזרי אונאה, פחות משתות אינו נחשב כלל, יותר משתות ביטול מקח. כי פגם האונאה הוא שמערב טוב ורע דהיינו שנפגם האמונהואין מבררת הניצוצות כנ"ל וזהו בחי' פגם הו' שהוא התורה בחי' מט"ט כנ"ל שהוא בחי' כשר ופסול וכו' וכנ"ל. וע"כ כל שהוא שתות חוזר כי בחי' מט"ט בחי' התורה הנ"ל נחלק לו' בחי' כשר ופסול וכו' כנ"ל, נמצא כשהפגם אין מגיע רק בבחי' חלק שתות ולא הגיע עדיין לבחי' היותר משתות דהיינו להפוך מכשר לפסול וע"כ ישנו בחזרה. אבל כשהפגם הוא בבחי' יותר משתות אזי הוא בחי' מערב טוב ברע כי מהפך מכשר לפסול וכו' כי בבחי' מט"ט בחי' התורה הנ"ל אין שם רק ו' בחי',שהם ששה חלקים לבד שהם כשר ופסול טמא טהור אסור ומותר ואין שייך שם חלקים יותר כי תיכף כשיוצא מכשר אזי הוא פסול וכו'. נמצא כל זמן שאין הפגם מגיע רק בחלק מששה שהוא שתות ועדין לא נגע יותר שהוא בחי' שפגם בבחי' אחת מהששה בחי' למשל בבחי' כשר ולא נגע יותר בגבול פסול, נמצא שעדין לא עירב כשר בפסול רק שהוא סוך לשם וע"כ חוזר. אבל תיכף כשהגיע הפגם יותר להלאה דהיינו יותר משתות נמצא שעירב כשר בפסול כי תיכף כשנוגע יותר משתות נוגע בפסול והוא בחי' מערב כשר בפסול וע"כ המקח בטל לגמרי כי המקח לא הי' רק לברר וכיון שאדרבא ע"י אותו המקח ערבם יותר ע"כ בטל לגמרי. אבל בפחות משתות אין נחשב כלל כי פחות מחלק ששה אינו נחשב כלל כי אין שם רק וא"ו בחי' כנ"ל:
segments.en: And similarly, conversely — one who blemishes the bris, G–d forbid, and is drawn after bodily desire, G–d forbid — which is kisufin of the sitra achra — then one begets souls that are not good, G–d forbid. And behold, in truth, regarding the holiness of the bris there are thousands and tens of thousands of levels. And certainly one must beseech Hashem, blessed be He, to merit guarding the bris in completeness — namely, to be separated and distinguished from this desire entirely, at the level of true tzaddikim, who are bound to Hashem, blessed be He, in kisufin d'kedushah constantly, as above. But nonetheless, not every person merits this, and the Holy One, blessed be He, does not come with tyranny against His creatures. And therefore, all children that one begets in a permissible manner according to the Torah — all of them are in the aspect of tikkun habris. For this is the essential tikkun habris — to beget children in the world, as above. And therefore, it is explained in the words of Rabbeinu of blessed memory that marriage is a tikkun habris, for all the marriages of Israel according to the law of our Holy Torah are all in the aspect of tikkun habris, as above. And therefore, the inheritance is due to the children. For all the money and parnasah is drawn from the children, who are the aspect of tikkun habris, as above — as is explained there in the Torah mentioned above, that through tikkun habris, everything toils for the sake of his parnasah, etc. — see there. For through his children, who are in the aspect of tikkun habris, receiving his inheritance and the fruit of his toil — through this, a repair is drawn for the soul of the deceased. And the more righteous and upright his children are, the greater the repair for the soul of the deceased. For the essential death is drawn from the sin of Adam HaRishon, who ate from the Eitz HaDa'as Tov VaRa [Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil] — through which death was decreed upon the world. And the essential sin of the Eitz HaDa'as is the matter explained in the Torah mentioned above — that one needs to be both a tzaddik and a lamdan. And one who considers that being a lamdan alone is a virtue — this is the aspect of Acher [Elisha ben Avuyah], who cut the plantings, because he considered that the angel Metatron in himself is an independent authority. For in truth, Metatron in himself, without the Holy One, blessed be He, is nothing and has no authority. So too, the Torah without good deeds is nothing — for if he has not merited, it becomes a potion of death for him, as all this is explained there in the Torah mentioned above. For one needs to include and unify the aspect of the “angel” with “Hashem of Hosts” — that bris tatah be included in bris ilah. That is, one should be both a tzaddik and a lamdan, as above. And one who is a lamdan alone and does not walk in the straight path — this is the aspect of the sin of the Eitz HaDa'as Tov VaRa. For the Eitz HaDa'as is the aspect of Metatron, as is known. This was the essential sin of Adam HaRishon — his sin was the sin of Acher, who cut the plantings, who separated the aspect of Metatron from Hashem of Hosts and denied the Essence, as is explained in the [holy] books. And therefore, death was decreed upon him, for from there the death is drawn. For through guarding the bris — which is the aspect of “the angel of Hashem of Hosts” — through this, one makes nefashos, which are the aspect of nekudos for the letters, and the letters are formed for good. And through this, one makes a bond between body and soul — which is the aspect of life. For the essential life is when the soul is connected with the body, and this is accomplished through holy yearnings, which are the aspect of nekudos for the letters — for it is all one: body and soul, and letters and nekudos. And according to how one forms the letters of the Torah for good through holy yearnings, which are the aspect of nefashos — so too one's soul is connected with one's body in a strong and mighty bond, until even after one's death, one's body is included in one's soul. For the tzaddikim are alive and endure forever, as our Sages of blessed memory said: “Tzaddikim in their death are called living” (Berachos 18a). And all this is merited through guarding the bris, through which they are called tzaddikim. For through guarding the bris in completeness, they merited to repair the blemish of the Eitz HaDa'as — for they include the aspect of Metatron, the aspect of the lamdan, within Hashem of Hosts, through their righteousness and their good deeds. And then the evil is separated from the Eitz HaDa'as. And then, through meriting guarding the bris, they make nefashos and enliven and form the letters for good, which were previously like a golem [unformed mass]. And so too, their body is formed for good, for it is all one, as above. For the essential thing is to break the body and compel it to yearn constantly for Hashem, blessed be He — for “today is to do them” (Devarim 7:11). For in the World to Come, certainly everyone will yearn for Hashem, blessed be He, alone, even the nations of the world. But “one who toiled on Erev Shabbos,” etc. For the essential thing is one who merits to yearn constantly for Hashem, blessed be He, the entire time that one's soul is bound in one's body — that one accustoms oneself to distance one's thought, that it should not think and contemplate, G–d forbid, desires and yearnings of this world, but only that it should yearn and long constantly for Hashem, blessed be He. And the more one yearns and longs for Hashem, blessed be He, and makes more nefashos for the letters — so too one draws holiness and vitality to one's body. For one's body, which is in the aspect of letters, is formed for good through the nefashos one has made, which are the vitality of the bodies that are the aspect of letters, as above. And therefore, through the children that one begets — who are the aspect of the nefashos that emerge through tikkun habris, as above — through them is the repair for the soul of the deceased, and it is considered as if he is alive, as our Sages of blessed memory said: “Whoever leaves a son to inherit him, it is as if he did not die” (Bava Basra 116a). For through the holy nefashos that he drew during his life through tikkun habris — through this, his soul is bound with his body forever, as above. For this is the aspect of the repair of the Eitz HaDa'as, which is the blemish of the bris, as above, through which death was drawn into the world, as above. And therefore, the children receive all his money and the fruit of his toil. For the money, which is a person's parnasah — which is the aspect of raglayim, as above — is the aspect of the body. For the vitality of the body is through eating and drinking. And one who eats with physical desire without kisufin d'kedushah — then one does not bind one's soul to one's body, and then when one's soul departs, one is truly dead, may the Merciful One spare us. But when one merits kisufin d'kedushah, through which one makes nefashos, as above — then all one's eating is in the aspect of lechem hapanim, where the eating ascends to the aspect of Panim. This is the aspect of the body being included in the soul — and not the reverse, G–d forbid. Therefore, one's soul is bound with one's body forever, even after death — for tzaddikim in their death are called living, through having merited kisufin d'kedushah while still in the body, through which one's body is included in one's soul forever, as above. And therefore, through the children — who are in the aspect of the nefashos that emerge through tikkun habris, as above — through their receiving his money and parnasah after his death, through this, his soul is elevated and illumination and vitality are drawn to his body in the grave. For the essential repair of the deceased is through the nefashos that are made through tikkun habris — through which the sin of the Eitz HaDa'as is repaired, and the contamination of death is repelled from the deceased, and the holiness of the nefashos that were made through tikkun habris is drawn upon him. Through these nefashos, he is called “living” even in death, in the aspect of: “Tzaddikim in their death are called living” — as above. And the essential inheritance belongs to the male son. For we need to yearn constantly for Hashem, blessed be He, with powerful yearning and longing. And then Hashem, blessed be He, also yearns for us. And through this, a yichud is made between Knesses Yisrael and the Holy One, blessed be He, and offspring are drawn forth — holy souls. As is explained there in the Torah mentioned above, the yearnings with which we yearn for Hashem, blessed be He, are the aspect of te'uvtih d'nukva [the desire of the female], etc. And the yearnings with which holiness reciprocates and yearns for us — this is the aspect of te'uvta did'chura [the desire of the male], etc. And afterward the nefashos are joined, etc. — see there. For this is a principle: the totality of Israel, and likewise the totality of all the worlds, are in the aspect of nukva [female/receiver] — the aspect of the recipient, relative to the Influencer and the Emanator, who is the Creator, blessed be His Name, who is the aspect of d'chura [male] relative to us. This is the aspect of the yichud accomplished through all the mitzvos — that Knesses Yisrael joins with her Beloved and is included in Him, blessed be He. And each person must see to it that he arouses himself first to yearn and to long for Him, blessed be He — that is'arusa d'l'sata should precede is'arusa d'l'eila. And then a great chesed is drawn upon him — which is the male side, in the aspect of: “When the woman emits seed first, she bears a male” (Berachos 60a). That is, when Knesses Yisrael yearns with great longing for Him until they give birth to nefashos, then Hashem, blessed be He, yearns for them and bestows upon them the light of the great chesed — which is the aspect of the male side, as is known. For when a person does not arouse himself on his own toward Hashem, blessed be He — then Hashem, blessed be He, yearns for him, for He, blessed be He, desires and longs that he return to Him. And then is'arusa d'l'eila precedes is'arusa d'l'sata, and then the nefashos that are born are in the aspect of the female side, the aspect of: “When the man emits seed first, she bears a female.” For the essential attribute of din, which is the aspect of the female side, is drawn from the beginning of the din of the creation of the world — whose essence was because in the beginning, at the time of the creation of the world, there was is'arusa d'l'eila without is'arusa d'l'sata, as is known and understood in the writings [of the Ari z”l]. And therefore, the essential inheritance belongs to the male son, for he is drawn from the aspect of the holy nefashos that are drawn from us to Him, blessed be He, as above — which is the essential tikkun of the nefashos, as above, from which all the parnasah and money is drawn, as above. But nonetheless, if he has no son: “And you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter” (Bamidbar 27:8). For since in any case offspring were brought forth and a soul of Israel was drawn into the world, it is all considered as tikkun habris, from which parnasah and money come. For the soul of the female is drawn from the aspect of is'arusa d'l'eila preceding is'arusa d'l'sata — from which is the hold of the din, which is the female side, as above. But nonetheless, it is a holy soul, since in any case one was aroused afterward and yearned for Hashem, blessed be He. The essential blemish entirely is when a person is not aroused to return to Hashem, blessed be He, and to yearn for Him, blessed be He, even when Hashem, blessed be He, arouses him and calls him through many kinds of proclamations and awakenings — and he pays no heed to this, G–d forbid. This is a complete rasha, who in his lifetime is called dead — since he has evil yearnings and is drawn after the desires of this world and is not aroused to yearn and to long for Hashem, blessed be He, even after is'arusa d'l'eila, as above. But one who in any case is aroused after is'arusa d'l'eila — who has begun to accustom himself to holy yearnings, and to incline his thought so that it does not think evil yearnings, but rather he accustoms himself to yearn and to long and to pine constantly for Hashem, blessed be He — then he too makes holy nefashos. And even though these nefashos are in the aspect of the female side, nonetheless they are in the aspect of tikkun habris. And therefore, the inheritance is due to the daughter where there is no son. For also the soul of the daughter is drawn from tikkun habris, from which the nefashos and the holy yearnings are drawn — from which comes all the parnasah, and the money is elevated to the aspect of Panim. This is the repair of the soul of the deceased — that his body be included in his soul, so that he is considered as if he is alive, as above. And therefore, when one has no children at all, G–d forbid, then one's wife needs yibum or chalitzah. And then: “She shall remove his shoe from upon his foot” (Devarim 25:9). The shoe — this is Metatron, which is the aspect of the Eitz HaDa'as, from which the essential death comes. The essential repair of death is through the children, who are in the aspect of tikkun habris, as above — through which Metatron is included in Hashem of Hosts, as above. Through this, one merits to make nefashos, and the letters are included in the nekudos, the bodies in the souls. And one merits the aspect of lechem hapanim — where the aspect of raglayim is included in the aspect of Panim. All this is one and the same aspect, as is explained to those who understand in the Torah mentioned above. And through this, the Torah mentioned above is well connected, and everything is embedded and joined and connected one with the other, as above. And then the contamination of death — the blemish of the Eitz HaDa'as — is sweetened, as above. But if one did not merit to beget souls in the world and died without children, G–d forbid — this is the aspect of the blemish of the bris. And then one's wife must perform chalitzah of the shoe — the aspect of Metatron — from upon his foot, so that the aspect of the foot of the one performing chalitzah, where the soul of the deceased is bound, as is brought — should return and ascend to the light of the Face, the aspect of: “And she shall spit in his face” (Devarim 25:9). And therefore the daughters of Tzelafchad argued: whichever way you look at it — if we are not considered progeny, let our mother undergo yibum. For certainly, if the daughters are not fit to inherit and to elevate his estate to the aspect of lechem hapanim — which is the repair of the deceased, as above — then certainly their mother would have needed to undergo yibum, in order to elevate the soul of the deceased through his wife, who is the aspect of raglayim, as is explained elsewhere, to the aspect of lechem hapanim. For the essential repair of death is through the feet ascending to the aspect of Panim, through which his sins are atoned, as above in the Torah mentioned above. For the body is the aspect of raglayim relative to the soul, which is the aspect of Panim. And when the raglayim — which is his estate that remains after him — ascend to the aspect of Panim, through his children who receive his inheritance — who are the nefashos that emerge through tikkun habris, from which comes the entire estate — through this, the body of the deceased is included in his soul. And this is his repair, as above. And certainly, it all depends on the nefashos and the children that one merits to leave behind, in accordance with one's tikkun habris and in accordance with one's holy yearnings — through all of which one's body is included in one's soul and is included in the light of life forever, as above. And this is what David HaMelech, peace be upon him, requested: “From the dead, by Your hand, Hashem… their portion is in life, and Your hidden treasure You fill their bellies; their children are satisfied, and they leave their surplus to their babes” (Tehillim 17:14). He requested to be among those dead whose portion is in life — who even after their death are called living. And this is through: “Your hidden treasure You fill their bellies.” “Hidden” [tzafun] — this is the aspect of “circlets of gold,” etc., the aspect of the pairing and combining of the letters through the nekudos, which is from the side of the north [tzafon], the aspect of: “From the north gold comes” (Iyov 37:22), as is explained there in the Torah mentioned above. And this is: “Your hidden treasure You fill their bellies.” “Their bellies” — this is the aspect of the letters of the Torah, in the aspect of: “And Your Torah is in my innards” (Tehillim 40:9). For the letters are the lowest level of the hierarchy of ta'amim [cantillation], nekudos [vowels], tagin [crowns], and osiyos [letters]. And their essential emergence is from the navel and below, which is the aspect of raglayim. And therefore, it is explained in the words of Rabbeinu of blessed memory that speech is the aspect of raglayim. And this is: “Your hidden treasure You fill their bellies” — that one merits to fill and to combine the letters of the Torah through one's holy yearnings, through which one makes nefashos. And through this: “their portion is in life,” as above. And this is: “Their children are satisfied, and they leave their surplus to their babes.” For the one depends on the other. For the children are drawn from the holy nefashos of the good yearnings, as above — on account of which the inheritance is due to the children, the aspect of: “And they leave their surplus to their babes” — for it is all one, as above. And this is: “I, in righteousness, shall behold Your face.” “Righteousness” [tzedek] — this is the aspect of raglayim, the aspect of the letters of speech, as it is written: “Righteousness shall walk before him” (Tehillim 85:14). That is: may I merit to elevate the raglayim to the aspect of Panim — which is the essential repair of death, as above. And this is: “I, in righteousness” — the aspect of raglayim — “shall behold Your face” — to elevate them to the aspect of Panim, in the aspect of: “Walk before Me” (Bereishis 17:1), as above — see all this in the Torah mentioned above well.
